diagnostic_evidence.quote: let $\alpha^{(1)},\beta^{(1)}\in\mathbb{R}^2$ the corresponding left singular vectors of $R_1$. Remind that the left singular vectors of $R_1$ constitute an orthonormal basis of $\mathbb{R}^2$.

issues.failure_explanation: Identifying the complex number w^(1)u with the vector R_1 u in R^2 and using the SVD of R_1 gives R_1u = sigma_1 c_1(u) alpha^(1) + mu_1 d_1(u) beta^(1) with alpha^(1), beta^(1) orthonormal in R^2. The displayed formula inserts an extra factor sqrt(-1) in front of the beta^(1) term. If alpha^(1), beta^(1) are read as complex numbers (as the ellipse description requires), then beta^(1) = ±sqrt(-1) alpha^(1), so sqrt(-1) beta^(1) = ∓alpha^(1) and the formula makes w^(1)u collinear with alpha^(1) for every u, contradicting the claim that W_1 is a (filled) ellipse and the subsequent orthogonality criterion (orthogonal) and the identities for OSF, which all presuppose the two components lie along perpendicular axes.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the factor sqrt(-1) in (w1u) (or state explicitly that alpha^(1), beta^(1) are regarded as complex numbers and write w^(1)u = sigma_1 c_1(u) alpha^(1) + mu_1 d_1(u) beta^(1)).
issues.overall_effect: The stated decomposition in Theorem euclidean0 is false as written; the later formulas (OSFOSF2, orthogonal, OSF1, point 2 after Theorem theorem9) are correct only under the corrected reading of (w1u).
issues.title: Decomposition (w1u) of the complex number w^(1)u contains a spurious imaginary unit inconsistent with the ellipse/orthogonality description
issues.why_classification: A local correction of one formula restores consistency; all downstream statements already use the corrected meaning, so nothing substantive is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For the initial ND $B(0)=0.61$ considered in Section 1, we have $K_{\infty}(y_{0},\widehat{z}_{0})=3.0035$.

issues.failure_explanation: By the paper's own formula (expression), for B(0)=0.60 one gets sqrt(1+0.36)/|−1+0.60| = 1.1662/0.4 = 2.9155, not 2.29. The value 3.0035 for B(0)=0.61 is consistent with the formula, so the 2.29 figure is a computational error.

failure_location.quote: we have $K_\infty(y_0,\widehat{z}_0)=2.29$ for $B(0)=0.60$, instead of $K_\infty(y_0,\widehat{z}_0)=3.00$ for $B(0)=0.61$.

issues.overall_effect: The numerical comparison in the Remark (available vs actual initial value) is misstated; the qualitative point of the Remark is unaffected.
issues.title: Reported asymptotic condition number for B(0)=0.60 in Remark is inconsistent with formula (expression)
issues.why_classification: Purely a local numerical correction with no effect on any result or conclusion.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Using the Euclidean norm as vector norm, we have $V_1=0.9988$ and $W_1=0.9986$.

issues.failure_explanation: The bound (epsilonc<) contains the term (1/2)log(1/(1−V_1)); with V_1=0.9988, r_1−r_2=1 and t̂=1 this equals (1/2)log(1/0.0012) ≈ 3.36. The example instead evaluates (1/2)log(1/sqrt(1−V_1)) ≈ 1.68, i.e. half of the term appearing in (epsilonc<), so the quoted contribution of V_1 to the onset bound is understated by a factor 2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the expression by (1/2)log(1/(1−V_1)) and the value 1.6844 by ≈3.36, consistent with (epsilonc<).
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative illustration of how V_1 close to 1 delays the onset in this example is misstated; the qualitative observation that the asymptotic behavior is quickly attained is unaffected.
